findings.title: Exported symbols changed without a breaking change notice
findings.body: The file now re-exports everything from `./react` instead of the previous mix of vanilla and React-specific exports. This is a **public API change** that should be accompanied by a major version bump and a changelog entry. Existing consumers importing `create`, `UseStore`, or `UseBoundStore` directly from `src/index.ts` will break at compile time.

findings.title: Import alias `createImpl` should be `createStore`
findings.body: The import alias `createImpl` on line 16 of `src/react.ts` is incorrect: the vanilla module now exports `createStore`, not `createImpl`. Using the wrong name will cause a runtime error when the module tries to call `createImpl(createState)` on line 74.

findings.title: Call to `createImpl` should be `createStore`
findings.body: The function call on line 74 uses the incorrect identifier `createImpl`, which no longer exists after the rename in `src/vanilla.ts`. This will throw a runtime ReferenceError. Replace it with the correct export name `createStore`.

findings.title: Default export renamed to `createStore` without updating references
findings.body: The default export in `src/vanilla.ts` was renamed from `create` to `createStore` on line 153, but the old name `create` is still referenced in the JSDoc type on line 53 and in the function signature on line 55. This mismatch will cause a runtime error when the type or function is used.

summary.problem: The refactor introduces multiple naming inconsistencies and a breaking public API change without a major version bump.
